status: prepared and unpublished; guild completion capture implemented, durable handoff still pending
scope: Completion events carry original trusted kill/repair time and detached qualifying guild runs. Capture each unique actual recipient's server-owned guild identity under its existing reward lock, without replay-time membership queries.
Keep a server-only guild display-name cache alongside existing public ID/tag. Refresh it from normal database-owned guild state; no new client authority, permission, registration or reward endpoint.

Repeat crystal-repair completions count active in-instance participants independently of whether their story quest advances. Departed/disconnected players remain excluded by existing repair eligibility. Duplicate player identities cannot qualify a guild alone.

Run duration uses original completion time. Mongo derives an omitted season from the recorded clear date, rejects an explicitly mismatched recorded season, preserves the fastest duration/largest member count and records the earliest clear through replay-safe min updates. Legacy callers without a recorded date retain their existing time default.

finalGameRace.scope: Final name-refresh/clear and single-emission assertions; snapshot duplicate/nonplayer/solo exclusion, detached captured membership and quarter-boundary times; actual four-player final-boss death handoff; repair completion with no active story quests; no internal names/runs in actor/event JSON. Direct handoff fixtures, not a full combat clear or wave-defense balance run.

disposableMongoRace.scope: Actual low-level leaderboard writes, identical replay, older slower clear, separate next-quarter clear and mismatched explicit season. Not a connected guild-membership or full dungeon session.
disposableMongoRace.isolation: Verified eidolon.qa.scope=guild-clear-capture-20261002, Mounts=[], loopback-only port32856,512MiB/32MiB tmpfs,1GiB memory and oneCPU. Ping confirmed before testing.
disposableMongoRace.cleanup: Stopped and removed only the exact inspected test container. Synthetic tmpfs leaderboard records are gone; production data/services and global Docker cache untouched.

remaining: Dungeon completion still schedules one database worker per event and lacks durable replay. This capture layer alone is not crash durability or a completion-worker bound. Next implement a typed private completion journal and one bounded replay consumer, with startup/shared-volume compatibility and failed-write/restart/acknowledgement checks.

Membership is captured from the server-owned world mirror when rewards/repair completion are credited; this is not a cross-store atomic proof against concurrent membership changes or delayed mirror updates. Review that boundary rather than claiming database membership-at-the-exact-kill transactionality.

Total journal disk limits, wider adversarial integration, account-recovery choice and ordered1.71/1.72 publication remain open. No deployment or full milestone acceptance is claimed; accepted live remains Alpha1.70.0.
